newsitem.title: JAPAN: Matsushita develops PD compatible DVD-RAM drives.
newsitem.headline: Matsushita develops PD compatible DVD-RAM drives.

text.p: Matsushita Electric Industrial Co said on Wednesday that it had developed DVD-RAM drives and disks based on a format agreed by ten DVD (digital video disk) developers earlier in April.
The announcement follows the Hitachi group, which also unveiled DVD-RAM drives and disks on Wednesday.
A Matsushita spokesman said the company's drives will be compatible with PDs, a rewritable computer disk with storage capacity of 0.65 gigabytes Matsushita developed in 1995.
DVD-RAM disks allow users to enter and rewrite 2.4 gigabytes of data and images, including motion pictures.
Matsushita plans sample shipments and volume production of DVD-RAM drives and disks after the summer, the spokesman said.

Toshiba Corp, which has played a major role in DVD's standarisation, said it plans to start sample shipments of its own products in the summer or autumn, while the official launch will be around December.
